newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-ASTLE POWERS NEW ZEALAND TO BIG SCORE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ASTLE POWERS NEW ZEALAND TO BIG SCORE.

text.p: Nathan Astle scored 117, his fourth century in one-day internationals, as New Zealand totalled 285 for seven in the opening match of the four-nation Independence Cup cricket tournament on Friday.

After Pakistani captain Rameez Raja had put New Zealand into bat, the 25-year-old Astle and fellow opener Bryan Young put on 155 off 145 balls against a straying Pakistani attack to register New Zealand's highest first-wicket stand in 48 one-day matches.
Astle's chanceless knock came off 132 balls, with two sixes and eight fours on a pitch which looked full of runs.
Young's 59 came off 65 balls and contained five boundaries before he was yorked by an inswinger from paceman Abdul Razzak.

Astle, having clouted leg-break bowler Shahid Afridi and left-arm spinner Mohammed Hussain for sixes over long-on, carried on to add 79 off 90 balls for the second wicket with Matthew Horne, who scored 45.
Astle was finally stumped by Moin Khan off Afridi and Horne followed soon after, bowled by off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq who took three for 38.
India and Sri Lanka are the other two teams in the tournament commemorating 50 years of India's independence from Britain.
